articles.description: Updated inactives and analysis based on the latest reports and official announcements leading up to kickoff.
articles.headlineJa: ファンタジー・フットボール第5週 不出場選手情報：カイル・モナンガイ、ラマー・ジャクソンが欠場
articles.descriptionJa: キックオフに向けて、最新のレポートと公式発表に基づいた不出場選手の最新情報と分析。
articles.body:
Whom should you start? Whom should you sit? To help you set your fantasy football lineups and avoid starting an offensive player who won't be in the lineup, we'll post fantasy-relevant updates and analysis here as NFL teams release their official inactives lists. 

Official Sunday inactives should begin coming in approximately 90 minutes before the scheduled kickoff times: around 11:30 a.m. ET for the early games and 2:30 p.m. ET for the late-afternoon games.

Refresh often for the latest information.

Don't forget to check these out: Mike Clay's Playbook | Week 5 Buzz 

Week 5 Rankings | Matchup rankings for Week 5

Biggest concerns heading into Week 5

Players in London

Dallas Goedert, TE, Eagles (knee): Goedert was able to return to practice this week, albeit in a limited fashion. But he will play in Week 5. He should operate as the top target for Jalen Hurts, especially in the red zone. Still, some names to play Goedert over this week are Brenton Strange, Dalton Schultz, and Michael Mayer.

Players with early starts

Ja'Marr Chase, WR, Bengals (concussion): Chase was able to practice this week and has a chance to suit up Sunday. Obviously, if Chase plays, you start him. If he sits, you can look at Dohnte Meyers, who saw nine targets last week, or Mitchell Tinsley, who saw seven. Mike Gesicki is also a potential "in-house" replacement option, as the Dolphins have allowed the fourth-most TE fantasy PPG.

Tee Higgins, WR, Bengals (adductor): Higgins was a DNP to start the week but returned to action in full Friday. He is questionable for this week. Fantasy managers should have a backup plan in place, just in case. As previously stated, you could go with Meyers and Tinsley -- but, ideally, there are more trustworthy options. Some receivers you should consider starting instead this week are Carnell Tate, Romeo Doubs and Denzel Boston.

Ashton Jeanty, RB, Raiders (ankle/foot): The Raiders' star RB popped up on the injury report Thursday after logging a limited session. He did not practice Friday and is now questionable for Week 5. Sure, if Jeanty plays for the Raiders, he starts for your fantasy football team.

However, if he sits, Mike Washington Jr. would be a borderline RB1 play. The "floor" is less certain for Washington -- run and check to see if he's still available on the waiver wire -- but the speedy, big-play threat brings a lot of upside. If he draws the start for Las Vegas, play him over Braelon Allen, David Montgomery, Omarion Hampton and Will Shipley.

Justin Jefferson, WR, Vikings (ankle): The star wideout returned to practice this week, and though he is questionable, he said the plan is for him to play. If Jefferson suits up, you play him in fantasy. If he sits, Jordan Addison should be viewed as a top-20 receiver.

articles.headline: Russell Westbrook wants to carry torch for L.A. Olympics
articles.description: Retired NBA player and Olympic gold medal winner Russell Westbrook said he wants to carry the torch when his native Los Angeles hosts the 2028 Games.
articles.headlineJa: ラッセル・ウエストブルック、ロサンゼルス五輪での聖火リレーを希望
articles.descriptionJa: NBA引退選手でオリンピック金メダリストのラッセル・ウエストブルックが、地元ロサンゼルスで開催される2028年大会で聖火を運びたいと語った。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Russell Westbrook won a men's basketball gold medal at the 2012 London Olympics, but the former NBA star has a new goal in retirement: to serve as a torchbearer when the 2028 Summer Olympics come to his hometown of Los Angeles.

"I'm putting this out now: I want to be in the presentation of Los Angeles, as it pertains to carrying the torch during the 2028 Olympics," Westbrook said Friday after being honored by the Los Angeles City Council for his community service work.

Westbrook, who announced his retirement in August after 18 NBA seasons, said that he has "challenged" his Why Not? Foundation employees to expand their philanthropic efforts to help achieve his goal.

"To be able to [carry the torch], you have to be able to position yourself to have your hands in so many different areas," he said. "For me, I'm working religiously impacting so many people, advancing technology, energy, education, health care, mental health and wellness. Every aspect, I want to have my hands in to help any way I can."

Westbrook's Los Angeles ties run deep: He attended Leuzinger High School and UCLA, then played for both the Lakers and Clippers during his decorated NBA career.

Los Angeles city councilwomen Heather Hutt saluted Westbrook as a "humanitarian" for his investments in local schools, athletic facilities and development projects.

"Anything I do from basketball to business is based around L.A.," he said. "I wear L.A. on my sleeve. The way I played, the way I operate, even the way I talk and walk is LA. I'll never change that. ... My legacy will be based on how much I give back to the people of L.A."

The nine-time All-Star and 2017 MVP retired as the NBA's all-time leader in triple-doubles. Westbrook, 37, averaged 15.2 points, 5.4 rebounds and 6.7 assists for the Sacramento Kings last season, and his decision to step away caught many by surprise given that he was still a productive player.

Houston Rockets forward Kevin Durant said Friday that Westbrook's retirement left him "a little sad."

"I thought Russ still had five or six more years left," Durant said of his longtime teammate on the Oklahoma City Thunder. "He's an athletic body that can still impact the game positively. Congrats to him on an iconic career."

Westbrook, who was known for his all-out energy on the court, has no intention of slowing down in retirement. While he said that his induction into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame will "hopefully happen soon," his primary focus is on his hometown.

"While I was playing, [Los Angeles] was my court," Westbrook said. "Basketball was something I was doing for fun. That was my outlet. Being drafted and being in the NBA was great. But ... being able to have more time, since my retirement, to give back more and be more present, that's more important."

articles.headline: Rams DT Aaron Donald practices in full, plans to play MNF
articles.description: Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald practiced in full Friday and said he plans to play Monday night against the Bills after missing Week 4 with back soreness.
articles.headlineJa: ラムズのDTアーロン・ドナルドがフル練習、MNFでの出場へ
articles.descriptionJa: ラムズのディフェンシブタックル、アーロン・ドナルドが金曜日にフル練習を行い、背中の痛みで第4週を欠場した後、月曜夜のビルズ戦に出場する意向を示した。
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald said he plans to play Monday night against the Buffalo Bills after missing Week 4 with back soreness.

Donald was listed as limited in practice Thursday but practiced in full Friday.

"I feel good," Donald said Friday after practice. "I feel a lot better than what I was."

On Thursday before practice, Rams coach Sean McVay said "the hope" is Donald would be able to play against Buffalo. McVay said the team would see how Donald responds to practicing, but "everything has been progressing in the right direction."

Donald said he hasn't had any setbacks during practice, before knocking on the podium.

Donald came out of retirement at the end of August after two seasons and did not play in the Rams' season opener. In two games this season, he had four tackles, a tackle for a loss and a quarterback hit. He has played 64 defensive snaps.

According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Donald has generated two pressures on 42 pass rushes this season, recording a 4.8% pressure rate that is his lowest through Week 4 since at least 2018 and the first time it has been below 10%.

In his 92 previous regular-season games from 2018 to 2023, Donald recorded one or fewer pressures in a game just three times. He has recorded one pressure in each of the two games he has played this season.

When asked whether he feels like he's in "football shape," Donald said he feels "good."

"I don't feel like my wind's off," Donald said. "I don't feel like I be out there exhausted. I think the way we able to rotate helped me a lot, but I do feel good. Just got to keep going, try to be more productive, do what I need to do."

articles.headline: Roberto De Zerbi: Dejan Kulusevski return can inspire Spurs at Man United
articles.description: Roberto De Zerbi has urged winless Tottenham to draw inspiration from Dejan Kulusevski's comeback ahead of Saturday's trip to Manchester United.
articles.headlineJa: ロベルト・デ・ゼルビ：デヤン・クルルシェフスキの復帰がマンU戦でのスパーズの刺激に
articles.descriptionJa: ロベルト・デ・ゼルビは、土曜日のマンチェスター・ユナイテッド戦を前に、未勝利のトッテナムに対し、デヤン・クルルシェフスキの復帰から刺激を受けるよう促した。
articles.body:
Roberto De Zerbi has urged winless Tottenham to draw inspiration from Dejan Kulusevski's comeback ahead of Saturday's trip to Manchester United.

Kulusevski has not played for Spurs in more than 500 days following a serious knee injury, but featured in a behind-closed-doors match during the international break and will travel to Old Trafford to offer support.

With Kulusevski inching closer to an emotional return after multiple setbacks and fears he may never play again, De Zerbi used the Swedish attacker as a reference point for bottom-of-the-table Tottenham, who have taken two points from their first five Premier League fixtures.

"Yes, he's an inspiration," De Zerbi said. "He reacted very well, with character, with courage, with passion. Yes, passion. It's a good word, passion. We have to take inspiration from Deki. I said the same in the meeting to the players.

"[Away at Old Trafford] he comes with us, also [Pedro] Porro [for support]. I want all players tonight and tomorrow, but he is working very well. I think he is an example for everyone, Dejan Kulusevski.

"Forget the player, but the example of how he reacted to the injury, the reaction to being unlucky, the character he showed this time, was an example, a reference for everyone."

Quizzed on when he could make his long-awaited return, De Zerbi explained: "I don't know, it's not just my responsibility.

"We are working together with the medical staff. They are working very well with him, they have done special work. We have to analyse week by week."

Spurs have sorely missed the creativity and character of Kulusevski during his 17-month absence, but De Zerbi is calm after a slow start to the campaign and was reminded of a similar situation for Aston Villa last season.

Asked about Villa being able to finish fourth after they went five games without a win, De Zerbi said: "Yes, it's possible. Why not? But to do what Villa did, we have to click.

"I think the first win is not a gift from God. You have to deserve to win. And we didn't deserve to win so far."

James Maddison will travel to Old Trafford and is available but De Zerbi hinted he might only have a cameo role after he missed days of training over the last week.

Major clubs across the world are circling playmaker Williams-Barnett, but Spurs have opened talks with the mercurial talent over a new deal, the Press Association reported.

De Zerbi acknowledged he was "thinking" about when to include Williams-Barnett in the squad after he made his second Tottenham appearance late on in the Carabao Cup win over Charlton.

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the analysis of each team's strength of schedule for the remainder of the season.

All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for games scheduled on days other than Sunday.

articles.headline: Arsenal 'very lucky' Mikel Arteta signed new deal, he is the 'best' - Declan Rice
articles.description: Declan Rice has said that Arsenal are "very lucky" to have the "best" coach in Mikel Arteta after the Spaniard signed a four-year contract, committing his future at the club.
articles.headlineJa: 「アーセナルはミケル・アルテタが新契約を結んだことは『非常に幸運』だ。彼は『最高』だ」 ― デクラン・ライス
articles.descriptionJa: ミケル・アルテタがクラブと4年契約を結び、将来を約束したことを受け、デクラン・ライスはアーセナルにとって「最高」の監督であるアルテタを擁していることは「非常に幸運」なことだと語った。
articles.body:
Declan Rice has said that Arsenal are "very lucky" to have the "best" coach in Mikel Arteta after the Spaniard signed a four-year contract to commit his future at the club.

Arteta has been in charge of the north London side since 2019, making him the longest-serving manager in England's top four leagues and will remain at Arsenal until 2030.

- Mikel Arteta signs new four-year Arsenal contract

In an exclusive interview with ESPN Brazil, Rice lauded the impact Arteta has had on Arsenal, having guided the Gunners to their first Premier League title in 22 years last season.

"It's just tactically, training, managing, the detail he goes into, the things he sees that you would never see," Rice told Renato Senise. "He's constantly watching you when you don't think you're being watched.

"He's watching, constantly asking questions to try and catch you out, to see if you're listening. He's always keeping you on your toes, making sure that you're ready.

"Every time we go into games, tactically we know what we're doing. Defensively, with the ball, how we're going to beat the opposition. It's just the fine details, the way he breaks everything down, which makes him the best for me.

"It's amazing that he [Arteta] signed a new contract and we get to have him as our manager for the next four years. So, we'll be very lucky."

Rice has started every game for Arsenal this season but withdrew from England duty during the international break to manage his workload.

The 27-year-old midfielder provided the positive update that he feels ready to play when the Premier League resumes this weekend.

"It's probably the first time, maybe the second time that I've ever missed a camp since I made my debut for England so I was gutted to miss the camp, but after an honest conversation with Thomas [Tuchel] and the boss here, it was the best thing for me to do, to settle down some of the issues that I've had," Rice said.

"And now I feel good, I feel fresh, and going into this next set of games, I'm going to feel really good."

- Viktor Gyökeres has shone for Sweden. Can he do it for Arsenal now?

- Premier League team news, injury updates after international break

 - Arsenal's Mikel Arteta: Premier League still best in the world despite Man City guilty verdict

Asked if the players felt different returning to the pitch this season as reigning champions, Rice insisted their title-winning campaign is in the past and they must focus on new challenges.

"It [winning the league] was an amazing achievement, but this year's a brand new season: New team, new opposition, new players. So it throws up a different challenge," Rice said. "So, yeah, OK, we are the champions, but we don't go on the pitch and think about last season.

"We're definitely playing with more confidence this season, you can feel that within the group, but it's about staying humble, and taking each game as it comes like we did last year and trying to win as many as possible."

articles.headline: 49ers DE Mykel Williams to make season debut vs. Seahawks
articles.description: 49ers defensive end Mykel Williams will make his 2026 debut Sunday against the Seahawks, a little less than a year after tearing his ACL and suffering meniscus damage in his right knee.
articles.headlineJa: 49ersのDEマイケル・ウィリアムズ、シーホークス戦で今季デビュー
articles.descriptionJa: 49ersのディフェンシブエンド、マイケル・ウィリアムズが日曜日のシーホークス戦で2026年シーズンの初出場を果たす。右膝のACL断裂と半月板損傷から、復帰まで1年足らずとなる。
articles.body:
SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- San Francisco 49ers defensive end Mykel Williams will make his 2026 debut Sunday against the Seattle Seahawks, a little less than a year after tearing his ACL and suffering meniscus damage in his right knee.

The 49ers will activate Williams, who returned to practice last week, from the physically unable to perform list on Saturday, coach Kyle Shanahan said. Although Williams is questionable on the injury report, he's slated to play.

"He's had a good two weeks," Shanahan said. "It was good last week, and this week's been even better. Ready to get him back out there on the field."

The Niners made a move to clear a roster spot for Williams on Friday, releasing defensive end Ogbo Okoronkwo, who could return to the practice squad.

Williams initially injured his knee on Nov. 2, 2025, in a game against the New York Giants. That ended his rookie season after just nine games in which he averaged 45 snaps per game and posted 20 tackles and a sack while working as an edge rusher on early downs and moving inside on obvious passing downs.

This week, Williams said he came back leaner and quicker once he recovered from the knee injury. Fellow end Nick Bosa helped Williams through his recovery as he, too, was going through a similar process.

Williams said it has been particularly hard watching the first four games this season as the Niners have lost Bosa (calf), defensive end Sam Okuayinonu (foot) and defensive tackles Alfred Collins (patellar tendon), C.J. West (knee) and James Thompson Jr. (high ankle sprain) to injuries.

"I'm losing my mind," Williams said. "I'm ready to go, though. I'm excited to play ball. I miss playing ball. It's been like a damn near a year since I played. I just want to get back on the field."

Williams plugs back into an end rotation that also has Keion White, Khalid Kareem and rookie Romello Height as options. Shanahan said Williams won't have any specific workload limitations as he returns.

"When he's out there, he'll be full go," Shanahan said. "We rotate our guys and understand it's his first game, but we've got to see how it goes."

Elsewhere on the injury report, Niners receiver Mike Evans (ribs) does not have a game designation and is good to go against the Seahawks. Bosa, Thompson, fullback Kyle Juszczyk (knee) and safety Marques Sigle are out.

Cornerback Upton Stout (shoulder) is questionable after practicing on a limited basis Thursday and but not Wednesday or Friday.

articles.headline: Fantasy football buzz: Expect Bears' Swift to retain RB1 role with Monangai out
articles.description: D'Andre Swift will be the Bears' RB1 with Kyle Monangai out, with Roschon Johnson potentially getting work.
articles.body:
Everything that happens in the NFL has additional context when viewed from a fantasy football perspective. From position battles to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values.

Our fantasy football buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers and our NFL Nation reporters, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around the league.

Oct. 9: What's next for Bears backfield with Monangai out?

By Courtney Cronin, NFL Nation

Ball security has been the focal point for Chicago Bears running back D'Andre Swift in the wake of two lost fumbles in three games. "That ain't me," Swift said, a sentiment coach Ben Johnson shares even after characterizing Swift's fumble Sunday against the New York Jets as "egregious."

There isn't much doubt that Swift will still be RB1 against the Green Bay Packers, however, particularly with Kyle Monangai ruled out of Sunday's game because of a turf toe injury. That means Roschon Johnson is next in line to split the run-game workload.

As the Bears aim to solve their red zone issues after going 4-for-13 since Week 1 (excluding kneel-downs), Johnson could be "part of the solution" to Chicago's goal-to-go struggles, given that he used to fulfill the short-yardage role prior to Ben Johnson's arrival. In 2024, Johnson had a career-high six rushing touchdowns, all of which came from inside the 10-yard line.

Oct. 9: Chase, Higgins practice, Bengals won't tip hand on availability

By Ben Baby, NFL Nation

Cincinnati Bengals wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase (concussion) and Tee Higgins (groin/neck) are officially questionable for Sunday's game against the Miami Dolphins. Both players were full participants at Friday's practice. While that is Cincinnati's lightest day of the week, it was the first time each player was a full-go at practice.

Bengals coach Zac Taylor didn't want to give any indication for their status on Sunday. Rookie Colbie Young (knee) is officially questionable as well. That means Dohnte Meyers could receive a sizable workload on Sunday. He had seven catches on nine targets for 82 yards in Week 4's loss to the Jaguars.

Oct. 9: Bucky Irving puts up 31.5 points on TNF

By Adam Rank

Not even the Cowboys could have seen this coming from Bucky Irving.

There are a lot of people who walk around trying to pretend like they saw the twist coming in "The Sixth Sense," "Fight Club" or maybe even "Meet the Parents." That seems more plausible than people who will claim they saw the Bucky Irving game coming. Impossible. I won't believe it. This Tampa Bay Buccaneers team was baaaad. Irving had scored just over six fantasy points in the previous game. Sean Tucker was stealing touchdowns. The Buccaneers were starting an undrafted quarterback.

But, it's the Dallas Cowboys. In primetime. Perhaps we should have seen it coming?

articles.body:
Chelsea are keeping an eye on Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong, while Scott McTominay's contract talks at Napoli have stalled, with Real Madrid reportedly interested in making a move. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Chelsea are monitoring Barcelona midfielder Frenkie de Jong's situation ahead of the January transfer window, reports Spanish outlet Sport. Barça will assess the 29-year-old's playing time as he returns from a knee injury, with increased midfield competition potentially limiting his opportunities. Chelsea remain attentive after sanctioning Enzo Fernández's move to Manchester City, while Barcelona have not ruled out any scenario. However, De Jong remains determined to stay and reclaim a starring role under Hansi Flick.

- Real Madrid have contacted Scott McTominay's representatives amid stalled contract talks with Napoli, according to Tuttomercatoweb. The Scotland midfielder could also attract approaches from Premier League clubs if an agreement remains elusive. Napoli may nevertheless block a January departure, keeping their star player for the remainder of the season while allowing themselves more time to negotiate an extension. As a result, any potential transfer is likely to be pushed back until next summer.

- Bayern Munich are monitoring Brighton & Hove Albion center back Luka Vuskovic, German journalist Christian Falk reports. The Croatia international is interested in joining Bayern, but the German champions would first need to offload Kim Min-Jae or Hiroki Ito to create space and funds for another defender. Vušković, who impressed on loan at Hamburg last season, remains on their shortlist, although Bayern are unable to make an offer as it stands.

- Real Madrid forward Endrick is open to joining AC Milan on loan in January, reports La Gazzetta dello Sport. The 20-year-old has indicated that Milan would be among his preferred destinations if Madrid sanctions a winter departure, having struggled for playing time this season. AS Roma and Aston Villa are also interested, but Milan could benefit from owner Gerry Cardinale's strong relationship with Endrick's representatives at Roc Nation. Any move remains dependent on Madrid's approval.

- Real Madrid expect Michael Olise to sign a new contract with Bayern, Sky Germany reports. Bayern have held preliminary talks over a contract extension as his current deal runs until 2029, with improved terms potentially making him the club's highest-paid player. A move to Madrid remains a possibility, but Olise is likely to stay if the Spanish giants do not make a concrete approach. Bayern may consider letting him leave the club if renewal talks fail.
